notes: The story switches to a flashback without signalling it: "He told his friends his story. / The sphere went down into black water." An A1 reader may think a second dive begins here. Consider opening the next paragraph with "In his story, the sphere went down into black water."
"Then some figures came to it." 'figures' (in the sense of shapes) is above beginner level; "Then some strange animals came to it." or "Then some strange people came to it." would be clearer.
"Hours went by." could be "They waited for many hours." for a true beginner; 'weight' and 'They put their heads down' are understandable from context.

issues.quote: Three friends were on board: Elstead, Weybridge and Steevens. He wanted to go five miles down, to the ocean bottom.
issues.problem: 'He' follows a list of three men, so the reader cannot tell who wanted to go down. Elstead has not yet been singled out at this level.
issues.fix: Three friends were on board: Elstead, Weybridge and Steevens. Elstead wanted to go five miles down, to the ocean bottom.

notes: "That night, Elstead told his friends his story. As the sphere went down..." works as a flashback marker; fine at A2.
No conditionals or passives found; 'would pull' / 'would float' are future-in-the-past, not conditionals.
"Its walls were thick enough to stand the great weight of the water above" uses 'stand' in the less common sense of 'withstand'; acceptable, but 'hold back' would be easier.
Genuinely literary register; the worship scene and the closing paragraph are well handled and faithful in spirit to Wells.

summary: A faithful, age-appropriate retelling of Wells's 'In the Abyss' across all five levels, with correct quizzes and good level grading. A2 fails on a single concrete issue: an ambiguous 'He' right after the list of three friends in the opening paragraph. A1 passes but would benefit from an explicit flashback marker and replacing 'figures'.
